stories.title: ProgramGym offers training environments for long-horizon coding agents
stories.summary: Researchers introduce ProgramGym, training environments where coding agents must discover requirements and design programs from scratch, rather than just fixing bugs in an existing repo.
stories.more: Most coding-agent work asks models to resolve issues in an existing repository or generate one from a given requirements document. ProgramGym instead gives agents less-defined, long-horizon tasks that require exploring a reference program before writing code, closer to how human engineers build software from scratch. The paper frames scalable, verifiable training environments for this setting as scarce compared to issue-resolution benchmarks. The excerpt does not specify which models were evaluated or how they performed.

stories.title: Paper formalizes 'Adversarial Heuristic Learning' for game-playing agents
stories.summary: A new paper formalizes Adversarial Heuristic Learning, where AI agents refine game-playing policies and supporting code from limited experience while keeping model weights fixed, tested in a long-running competition.
stories.more: Adversarial games have long driven progress from heuristic search to reinforcement learning, but adapting strategies from only a few samples remains difficult. The authors propose Adversarial Heuristic Learning (AHL), a paradigm where AI agents act as learning engines that revise game policies and supporting software instead of updating model weights. They test the approach in a long-running game agent competition to see whether agents can climb the standings over time. The excerpt does not detail which games or opponents were used, or the measured improvement.

stories.title: VisionWeave gives multimodal LLMs elastic, content-adaptive visual tokens
stories.summary: VisionWeave lets multimodal large language models give more visual detail to regions that need it and less to simple areas, aiming to cut the cost of dense, fixed-size patch tokens.
stories.more: Multimodal LLMs typically encode images into dense, fixed-size patch tokens, which is costly because visual information is unevenly distributed across a scene. Existing token-pruning and adaptive methods are limited in how finely they adjust granularity, generalize across tasks, and integrate with the base model. VisionWeave instead builds elastic visual representations as a native capability of the MLLM itself, rather than as a separate pruning step. The excerpt does not specify benchmark results or which base models were tested.

stories.title: StereoBind adds spatially consistent stereo audio to video-audio generation
stories.summary: Researchers propose StereoBind, which keeps generated stereo audio's perceived sound location consistent with on-screen motion, aiming to make joint video-audio generation more immersive for AR/VR and gaming.
stories.more: Joint video-audio generation models already achieve strong semantic correspondence and temporal synchronization between sound and picture. But applications like AR/VR and interactive gaming also need stereo audio whose perceived location shifts correctly as the visual source moves, a property the authors call Dynamic Spatial Correspondence. Prior work has largely overlooked this requirement. StereoBind is introduced as a framework targeting that gap, though the excerpt does not describe its architecture or evaluation results.

stories.title: EmbodiedCLBench benchmarks continual learning for embodied, self-evolving agents
stories.summary: A new benchmark, EmbodiedCLBench, tests how well embodied agents can accumulate experience and transfer it to new tasks in simulation, extending continual-learning research beyond non-embodied settings.
stories.more: Continual learning asks models to retain past experience and apply it to new tasks, but most existing research has stayed in non-embodied settings. EmbodiedCLBench is presented as the first benchmark to evaluate continual learning specifically for self-evolving embodied agents in simulation. Its core evaluation principle is compositional generalization, testing whether agents can recombine learned skills in new combinations. The excerpt does not detail the simulation environments used or report specific results.

stories.title: SoloQ brings calibration-free low-bit quantization to diffusion language models
stories.summary: SoloQ is a new quantization method for diffusion language models that skips the calibration step, aiming to cut the memory and compute costs of deploying these increasingly popular models.
stories.more: Diffusion large language models are a growing alternative to autoregressive LLMs, generating text through bidirectional diffusion rather than next-token prediction. Their large size and high inference cost make low-bit weight-activation quantization attractive, but existing quantization approaches reportedly fall short for this architecture. Full-sequence denoising requires repeated compute-heavy forward passes, and block-diffusion variants add a memory-intensive KV-cache on top. SoloQ is proposed as a calibration-free quantization method to address these costs, though the excerpt cuts off before describing results.

According to the report, some of Silicon Valley's most powerful people are nonetheless falling in line and using Trump's preferred term. The broader public, however, is reportedly sticking with the familiar 'AI' label. The excerpt does not name which executives or companies have adopted the new term.

stories.title: TechCrunch debates whether dropping NDAs could ease data center opposition
stories.summary: On TechCrunch's Equity podcast, hosts discuss the fallout from data center moratoriums and whether the AI industry's use of NDAs is worsening its communication problem with opponents.
stories.more: The episode covers the impact of local moratoriums on new data center construction, a growing flashpoint as AI's compute demands drive rapid buildout. Hosts debate whether the AI industry has a broader communication problem with communities and officials opposing these projects. One specific question raised is whether ending the use of NDAs around data center deals could help persuade opponents. The excerpt does not detail which moratoriums or deals are being discussed.

stories.title: SoftwareGym synthesizes diverse software environments to train computer-use agents
stories.summary: SoftwareGym is a new automated pipeline that synthesizes varied GUI software environments to train computer-use agents at scale, addressing limited coverage in native and browser-based training setups.
stories.more: Computer-use agents are improving quickly, but building diverse, reliable software environments to train them remains a bottleneck. Native application environments take significant effort to construct and integrate, which limits coverage and risks overfitting to specific apps, while browser-hosted environments offer only limited interaction depth and workflow complexity. SoftwareGym is introduced as an automated pipeline for synthesizing GUI software environments to scale training beyond these constraints. The excerpt does not specify how many environments were generated or how trained agents performed.
